modelResponse.episodeSummary: An 82-year-old female with a history of atrial fibrillation (AFib) on digoxin presented with nausea, vomiting, and visual disturbances. Her heart rate slowed to 38 bpm with a regular rhythm, transitioning from AFib. She exhibited ECG changes consistent with digoxin effect and mild symptoms with stable hemodynamics.
modelResponse.mostLikelyEtiologyAndClinicalContext: Digoxin toxicity is the most likely etiology, causing excessive AV nodal blockade leading to junctional bradycardia. This is supported by the toxic digoxin level (3.8 ng/mL), symptoms of nausea and vomiting, visual disturbances (yellow-green halos), and ECG findings of scooped ST segments ('digoxin effect'). The regular rhythm despite a history of AFib suggests AV junctional takeover, a common manifestation of digoxin toxicity.
